Yangtzepoo Station.
8th December 1922.

REPORT ON Russian ("White") Refugees.

Made by D. T. Corbutt Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

I beg to report that a telephone message
was received from D.I. Sullivan at 11.05 a.m. 8-12-22
stating that a Russian ship named "Tres," was on its way
up river carrying refugees and was likely to anchor opposite
this District. At 12 noon the Ship was located,
anchored in the river between Lichang Road Jetty and the
C.S. Tug Lower Dock. She is a very small vessel,
probably about 30 or 40 tons and no bigger than the tender
"Alexandria" if as large. She had on board about 80
men and female refugees who landed at Lichang Road Jetty
and the Japanese Engineering Yard & T'sao Road about
12.30 p.m. and proceeded towards Hongkew on foot. They
appeared to be a good type of people all dressed in clean
clothes. I ascertained that the boat had come directly from
Hankow up the river to Shanghai to discharge its passengers
and that she brought people from one of the other boats
lying off Woosung. I am informed that it is only
carrying 71 officers and men, including crew and passengers.
The rest are women & children.

Yours faithfully,

[Signature]
D.T. Corbutt.
Sgt.

1922年12月8日。

关于俄国（“白俄”）难民的报告。

由 D. T. Corbutt 撰写，经 [签名] 转呈

先生，

谨此报告，本人于1922年12月8日上午11时05分接到警探长（D.I.）沙利文（Sullivan）的电话留言，称一艘名为“Tres”号的俄国船只正载着难民溯江而上，很可能在本辖区对岸抛锚。中午12时，该船被定位，停泊在黎昌路码头与招商局拖轮下坞之间的江面上。这是一艘非常小的船只，吨位可能约为30或40吨，即使算大也不超过“Alexandria”号交通艇的大小。船上约有80名男女难民，他们于下午12时30分左右在黎昌路码头以及日本工程 yard 和曹家渡路（T'sao Road）登陆，随后步行前往虹口。他们看起来都是体面的人，衣着整洁。经查证，该船直接从汉口溯江而上抵达上海以卸下乘客，且其人员来自另一艘停泊在吴淞外的船只。据告知，该船仅载有71名军官和士兵，包括船员和乘客。其余为妇女和儿童。

此致，

[签名]
D.T. Corbutt。
警长。

December 8, 1922.

REPORT ON Russian refugees at Woosung.

Made by J. I. Sullivan. Forwarded by [Signature] Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,
Three more ships with Russian refugees on board arrived at Woosung on December 8 making altogether twelve ships now at Woosung. The names of two of the ships are the "Strelok" which has on board a crew of 70 men and also 96 passengers, and the S. S. "Uliss" which has a crew of 47 men and 71 passengers. The name and particulars concerning the one other ship have not yet been obtained. The total number of persons on board eleven of the twelve steamers is 1547.

Rear Admiral Stark has been living ashore at 67 Broad way Terrace since December 7. When interviewed by a Police representative on the night of December 7 he stated that he had not received any instructions from the authorities as regards his ships except that he has been told by the Assistant Commissioner for Russian Affairs that the matter has been referred to Peking. Admiral Stark states that he has an appointment to meet Mr. Hillman, Deputy Coast Inspector, Chinese Maritime Customs, on board the S. S. "Baikal" on December 9.

Admiral Stark states that his fleet consisting altogether of 27 ships left Vladivostok on October 27. They went first to Possiet, near the Korean frontier, where they stayed a few days, then to Fusan, Korea, where they stayed three weeks, then to Chefoo, China. Five of the steamers which formed the nucleus of the Russian Volunteer Fleet were left at Fusan, three small launches were sold, and two of Rear Admiral Stark's small steamers were left at Yentai leaving fifteen vessels sailing under the orders of Admiral Stark. There are altogether 171 per-

关于吴淞俄国难民的报告。

由 J. I. Sullivan 撰写。经 [签名] 刑事情报处处长转呈。

先生，
12月8日，又有三艘载有俄国难民的船只抵达吴淞，使得目前在吴淞的船只总数达到十二艘。其中两艘船的名字是“Strelok”号，船上有70名船员以及96名乘客；另一艘是“Uliss”号轮船，有47名船员和71名乘客。第三艘船的名称及详情尚未获取。这十二艘轮船中的十一艘上的人员总数为1547人。

斯塔克（Stark）海军少将自12月7日以来一直居住在百老汇路公寓（Broadway Terrace）67号的陆上住所。12月7日晚，当警方代表与其会面时，他表示除被告知俄国事务助理专员称此事已上报北京外，他未收到当局关于其船只的任何指示。斯塔克海军少将表示，他已约定于12月9日在“Baikal”号轮船上会见中国海关副海岸视察员希尔曼（Hillman）先生。

斯塔克海军少将表示，他的舰队共由27艘船只组成，于10月27日离开符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。他们首先前往靠近朝鲜边境的波西耶特（Possiet），停留了几天，然后前往朝鲜釜山（Fusan），停留了三周，之后前往中国烟台（Chefoo）。组成俄国志愿舰队核心的五艘轮船被留在釜山，三艘小型汽艇被出售，斯塔克海军少将的两艘小型蒸汽船被留在烟台（Yentai），留下十五艘船只受斯塔克海军上将指挥航行。共有171人——

sons on those fifteen steamers made u as follows:- The crews
and their families 200, marines 300, cadets from two corps
and their families 600. There are approximately 350 women
and children on board the ships. The fleet left Tusan on
December 3 and on the way to Shanghai they encountered a severe
storm and Admiral Stark states that he is fairly sure of the
safety of one of the missing ships but he is afraid the other two
have been wrecked . He states that many of the men on the
ships are technical men for instance on is an engineer who
built the port, harbour, and fortifications of the port
of Reval. He proposes to let anyone who can obtain a
position stay in Shanghai. The officers are the cause of most
anxiety. Admiral Stark states that in his opinion no harm
would come to them if they returned to Vladivostock but they
refuse to return. He states that all the people on the ships
are practically destitute.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

D. C. I.

D. C. I.

在这十五艘轮船上，人员构成如下：船员及其家属200人，海军陆战队300人，两个学员队及其家属600人。船上大约有350名妇女和儿童。舰队于12月3日离开釜山（Tusan，原文如此，应为Fusan），在前往上海的途中遭遇猛烈风暴，斯塔克海军少将表示，他相当确信其中一艘失踪船只的安全，但担心另外两艘已失事。他表示，船上的许多人都是技术人员，例如其中一位是建造雷瓦尔（Reval）港口、海港和防御工事的工程师。他提议让任何能找到工作的人留在上海。军官们是最令人担忧的原因。斯塔克海军少将表示，在他看来，如果他们返回符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock，原文拼写错误），不会受到伤害，但他们拒绝返回。他表示，船上的人实际上都身无分文。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，

REPORT ON Russian refugees.

Made by D. L. Sullivan. Forwarded by [Signature] D.S.

Sir,

Four more ships of Rear Admiral Stark's fleet arrived at Woosung during December 7 making nine ships in all which are now anchored at Woosung. The "S. S. 'Batarer', 'Fervator' and 'Bol'ol'" are described as gunboats and one ship is described as a transport on the Customs list. Mr. Grosse, Assistant Commissioner for Russian Affairs when interviewed on December 7 stated that there are altogether fifteen ships in Admiral Stark's fleet, some of which are very small, in fact only steam launches, and the remaining six vessels are expected to arrive at Woosung during the next couple of days. Mr. Grosse states that he told the Chinese authorities and the Consular Body, that the fleet would in all probability come to Shanghai. He states that he cannot possibly assist the refugees who are on board the vessels as he already has as much as he can do to help the Russian refugees who are already here. He has informed the Chinese authorities of his inability to take any responsibility for the feeding and housing of the latest arrivals and in consequence the Chinese Authorities have wired to Peking for instructions and have ordered that the refugees be not allowed to land until a reply is received from the capital. In the meantime they are all on board the ships.

Mr. Grosse states that there are approximately 1051 refugees on board the fifteen vessels. They desire to go to Servia or Czecho-Slovakia, but the transporting of so many people to Europe would be a very expensive business. DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

FILED
Shanghai, December 7 192 .

Sir,

As a result of my telephone inquiry to the Arsenal
at 3.40 p.m. December 7, I beg to report having learnt
from Magistrate Duff that according to reports that
have reached the Governor two Japanese warships each
carrying over 100 Russian refugees had arrived beyond
Woosung, that more vessels of that description are
expected and that the Governor had issued an order to
the Marine Police to see that none of the Russians
are permitted to land at Woosung and that no one from
the shore be allowed to go on board. There is, however,
no truth in the report that the Woosung forts have
received instructions from the Governor to fire on
the ships. The Bureau for Foreign Affairs has wired
to the Tai O Tao Yu asking for information but
no reply has yet been received. The Governor,
Mr. Duff further stated, quite realizes the impossibility
of permitting the landing of any further Russians on
the Settlement as might lead to the presence
of numerous disloyal Russians in any quarter and
it is a menace to peace and good order.

Your obedient servant,

J Burnside
for D. G. I.

Commissioner of Police.

REPORT ON Russian Refugees

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by J. P. Evans R. I.

Sir,

D. C. Ropes reports that two of Admiral Starks
flotilla, gunboats named the "Battery" and "Baikal" arrived
at Woosung on the night of December 5. They have on board
two companies of marines and one cadet corps who are refugees
from Vladivostock. D. C. Ropes further reports that ten
more ships of Admiral Stark's fleet, which originally consisted
of about 30 ships altogether, are expected to arrive at
Woosung during the forenoon to-day. There are reported
to be seven thousand refugees on board the ten ships.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. I.
